title: 小儿垂钓
author: 胡令能
intro: A scruffy little boy is fishing by the water. When a passer-by asks him the way, he just waves — he won’t say a word in case he scares the fish. A sweet, funny snapshot of a child at play.
analysis: 这首诗写一个乡下小孩学钓鱼，像一张生动的照片。前两句写外貌和动作：头发乱蓬蓬的小孩，侧着身子坐在长满青苔的岸边，野草遮住了他的身体。“蓬头”写出孩子的天真，不讲究打扮；“侧坐”说明他坐得很随便，心思全在鱼竿上。后两句写一个小故事：有路人过来问路，小孩远远地向他招手，却不出声回答——原来他怕说话会把鱼吓跑。一个“怕”字，把孩子认真又可爱的样子写活了。诗人没有直接说孩子多么专心，而是用招手不说话这个细节让读者自己感受，这就是古诗常说的“以动作写心理”。全诗语言浅显，充满生活情趣。
analysisEn: This poem is like a lively snapshot of a country boy learning to fish. The first two lines give his look and posture: hair a tangled mess, he sits sideways on a mossy bank, half hidden by the long grass. “Tousled hair” shows a child who doesn’t care about looking neat; “sitting sideways” shows he has plonked himself down anyhow — all his attention is on the line. The last two lines tell a tiny story. A passer-by comes along and asks for directions. The boy waves from a distance but doesn’t answer, because he is afraid that speaking will frighten the fish away. That one word 怕 (“afraid”) brings his serious, adorable little face to life. The poet never says “the child was concentrating”; he lets one gesture — a wave instead of a reply — show us what is going on in the boy’s head. The language is simple and full of everyday charm, which is why Chinese children love this poem.
background: Hu Lingneng (c. 785–826) was a Tang poet of humble background who is said to have mended pots and pans for a living before turning to poetry, then lived as a recluse. Only a handful of his poems survive, and this is the best known.
pronunciation: “稚子”的“稚”读 zhì；“垂纶”的“纶”读 lún（钓鱼线），不读 guān；“莓苔”读 méi tái。“不应人”的“应”读 yìng（回应）。“怕得鱼惊”的“得”读 dé。“应”有的旧注读 yīng，网站按通行注音读 yìng。
version: 采用通行教材版本。异文：《万首唐人绝句》作“倒坐莓苔草映身”“恐畏鱼惊不应人”，教材作“侧坐”“怕得”，网站从教材。

lines.py: péng tóu zhì zǐ xué chuí lún
lines.lit: A tousle-haired child learns to dangle a fishing line;
lines.en: A boy with tangled hair is learning to fish,

lines.py: cè zuò méi tái cǎo yìng shēn
lines.lit: sitting sideways on moss, grass shading his body.
lines.en: perched sideways on the moss, half hidden in the grass.

lines.py: lù rén jiè wèn yáo zhāo shǒu
lines.lit: A passer-by asks the way; from afar he waves his hand,
lines.en: When a stranger asks the way, he only waves from afar —

lines.py: pà dé yú jīng bù yìng rén
lines.lit: afraid the fish will be startled, he doesn’t answer the man.
lines.en: he won’t say a word, in case he scares the fish.

words.note: 现代汉语有成语“蓬头垢面”。
现代汉语说“小孩”；“稚”还在“幼稚”“稚嫩”里用。

words.en: to dangle a fishing line; to fish
words.note: 纶：钓鱼用的丝线。现代汉语说“钓鱼”。
这里是“遮掩”的意思，和今天“反映”“映照”不同。
古代问路的客气话，现代汉语说“请问”。

imagery.name: 鱼
imagery.zh: 看不见的鱼是全诗的中心：孩子的一举一动都围着“别吓跑鱼”。
imagery.en: The unseen fish are the centre of the poem: everything the boy does is about not scaring them away.

imagery.name: 苔
imagery.zh: 长满青苔的岸边，说明这里安静偏僻，少有人来。
imagery.en: A mossy bank tells us the spot is quiet and out of the way, rarely visited.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 野草遮住孩子的身子，写出乡野的自然，也像孩子在“埋伏”等鱼。
imagery.en: The wild grass half-hides the boy — natural countryside, and almost as if he is lying in ambush for the fish.
